title: Ambra Grisea
text: This remedy is characterized by a general nervous hypersensitivity and a feeling of embarrassment and shyness. It is useful in cases of nervous disorders and digestive disturbances in elderly people. There is a general feeling of weakness and lack of vital force. The patient is often a thin, nervous person. There is a marked tendency to premature old age. Shy and embarrassed. Aversion to the presence of others. Confused and forgetful. Loquacity. Anxiety. Headache, with a sensation of weight in the forehead. Vertigo on rising. Scalp feels tight. Eyes red and burning. Dimness of vision. Deafness. Tinnitus. Dryness of the mouth. Tongue feels dry and sticky. Foul breath. Appetite poor. Thirst. Heaviness and pressure after eating. Eructations. Distended with gas. Rumbling. Flatulence. Constipation. Stool large and hard. Frequent desire for stool. Frequent desire to urinate. Scanty urine. Shortness of breath on motion. Violent cough, ending in eructations. Hoarseness. Palpitation, with a sensation of oppression in the region of the heart. Restless. Sleeplessness from nervousness. Twitching and jerking of the muscles. Trembling of the hands. Numbness and tingling. Itching and burning. Dry and scaly. Worse in the presence of others and in the morning. Better from open air and cold food. Compare: Moschus; Phosphorus; Valeriana. Third to thirtieth potency.
